beats.narration: I cannot believe, she stated, that my brother ordered such crimes.
Yet classified wartime archives revealed a darker connection.
Paula had been secretly engaged to Doctor Erwin Jekelius.
Jekelius was a chief organizer of the Aktion T4 extermination program.

beats.narration: Under his direction, thousands of psychiatric patients were systematically murdered.
Over thirty-two hundred patients were transferred to Hartheim Castle.
Behind closed gates, industrial gas chambers operated in absolute secrecy.
Among those murdered was Aloisia Veit, a cousin of the Hitler family.
The machinery of death consumed even relatives of the dictator himself.
Following months in custody, Paula was cleared of criminal guilt.

beats.narration: The Bavarian state confiscated all properties and publishing rights.
Penniless, she survived on welfare and the charity of local acquaintances.
In 1959, she gave her only recorded television interview.
One year later, on June 1st, 1960, she died in Berchtesgaden.
She was buried under the name Paula Wolff in the mountain cemetery.
With her death, the immediate bloodline of Adolf Hitler came to an end.
